cards.explanation: The answer is False. Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, did evil in the sight of the LORD, “…but not like the kings of Israel who preceded him.” (2 Kings 17:2) So the kings before him were the ones who set the bar, friends. Hoshea still did evil, just not like them.

The answer is True, friends. Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, found out that Hoshea “…had not paid tribute to the king of Assyria as in previous years.” (2 Kings 17:4) Hoshea had also conspired to send envoys to King So of Egypt. That's like skipping your rent and then plotting to send a representative over to a different landlord.

The answer is that he arrests Hoshea and puts him in prison, friends. When the king of Assyria discovered the plan with Egypt and the missing tribute, that's what he did. (2 Kings 17:4) No second chances were offered, at least not in the text. When you skip the payment AND write to the neighbors, the news travels.
The answer is that he besieges it for three years, friends. The king of Assyria marched up to Samaria and besieged it. (2 Kings 17:5) That's three whole years.

The answer is that the king of Assyria captures it, friends. In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria. (2 Kings 17:6) The siege that began in verse 5 led to this. Samaria was taken.

The answer is the Medes, friends. The king of Assyria settled the Israelites in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes. (2 Kings 17:6) The Medes were a people living in cities of their own. The verse lists three places, and this is the third.

The answer is Egypt, friends. The writer says the LORD brought Israel out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt. (2 Kings 17:7) It's a reminder of what the LORD had already done for them. The writer starts here before listing everything they did.

The answer is True, friends. The writer says all this happened because Israel had sinned against the LORD their God, and “They had worshiped other gods” (2 Kings 17:7) That's the start of the writer's explanation. The list gets longer from here.

The answer is on every high hill and under every green tree, friends. The Israelites “…set up for themselves sacred pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.” (2 Kings 17:10) Every high hill, every green tree. That's a lot of places, and the writer wants us to see how many.

The answer is to turn back and keep His commandments, friends. The LORD told them through His prophets and seers, “Turn from your wicked ways and keep My commandments and statutes…” (2 Kings 17:13) It was a call to come back. The warning came before the exile, not after.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, “But they would not listen…” (2 Kings 17:14) The LORD had sent warning after warning, and they didn't listen. They stiffened their necks like their fathers.

The answer is not to imitate them, friends. They went after “…the surrounding nations that the LORD had commanded them not to imitate.” (2 Kings 17:15) So the command was about not copying them. And they copied them anyway.
The answer is two cast idols of calves, friends. The text says they “…made for themselves two cast idols of calves and an Asherah pole.” (2 Kings 17:16) Two calves, plus the pole.

The answer is True, friends. The writer says they “…devoted themselves to doing evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.” (2 Kings 17:17) It's a heavy verse, and the writer doesn't soften it. I think it's one to read slowly.

The answer is Judah, friends. The LORD was very angry with Israel and removed them from His presence, and “Only the tribe of Judah remained…” (2 Kings 17:18) Judah was the one left. The writer goes on to say what happened with Judah next.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, “…even Judah did not keep the commandments of the LORD their God, but lived according to the customs Israel had introduced.” (2 Kings 17:19) So Judah followed Israel's customs. The writer doesn't let Judah off the hook.

The answer is that he leads them away from following the LORD, friends. Jeroboam son of Nebat, the king Israel made, “…led Israel away from following the LORD and caused them to commit a great sin.” (2 Kings 17:21) He led them the wrong direction, away from the LORD. The writer is going back to where it started.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, “The Israelites persisted in all the sins that Jeroboam had committed and did not turn away from them.” (2 Kings 17:22) So Jeroboam's sins carried on through the generations. The people never turned away.

The answer is through all His servants the prophets, friends. The LORD removed Israel from His presence “…as He had declared through all His servants the prophets.” (2 Kings 17:23) So the word had come through the prophets. They had declared it ahead of time.
